The Landolt C chart is typically used to assess central visual acuity, while the Snellen E chart is used for peripheral or distance vision. In cases of strabismus amblyopia, patients may experience a slight overestimation of their visual acuity on the Snellen E chart due to differences in their visual field and ocular alignment.

However, it's essential to consider that small variations in visual acuity can occur even within individuals with the same level of strabismus. This highlights the complexity of evaluating visual function in patients with amblyopia.

In summary, while there may be some discrepancies between Landolt C and Snellen E acuity scores in certain cases of strabismus amblyopia, these differences are likely due to individual variations rather than a general decline in overall vision.
